Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.

# Labour Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Core Priorities

The manifesto establishes five national missions: economic growth, clean energy, crime reduction, breaking barriers to opportunity, and NHS reform.

## Economic Policy

Labour commits to fiscal rules requiring balanced day-to-day budgets and falling debt by the fifth forecast year. Corporation tax will be capped at 25%. The party pledges no increases to Income Tax, National Insurance, or VAT.

Key economic initiatives include:
- A National Wealth Fund (£7.3 billion) for industrial investment
- An Industrial Strategy Council on statutory footing
- Business rates reform in England
- A ten-year infrastructure strategy
- Planning system overhaul to enable 1.5 million new homes
- Rail nationalisation as contracts expire
- Skills England to coordinate workforce training

## Energy and Environment

Great British Energy, a publicly-owned company headquartered in Scotland, will receive £8.3 billion. Targets include zero-carbon electricity by 2030 through expanded wind, solar, and nuclear power. The Warm Homes Plan allocates £6.6 billion for home energy upgrades. No new oil and gas exploration licences will be issued, though existing licences continue.

## Public Services

NHS reforms include 40,000 additional weekly appointments, doubled CT/MRI scanners, 8,500 mental health staff, and workforce planning publication. Social care will move toward a National Care Service with national standards.

Education commitments include 6,500 new teachers, 3,000 primary school nurseries, free breakfast clubs, and curriculum review. Private school VAT exemptions end.

## Security and Immigration

Defence spending will reach 2.5% GDP with a Strategic Defence Review. A Border Security Command replaces the Rwanda scheme. The asylum backlog will be cleared with additional caseworkers and a returns enforcement unit.

## Crime and Justice

Neighbourhood policing receives thousands of new officers. Knife crime measures include ninja sword bans and youth intervention programmes. Violence against women receives specialist rape units in every police force.

## Constitutional Reform

Hereditary peers lose voting rights. A mandatory retirement age of 80 applies to Lords members. Voting age drops to 16. An Ethics and Integrity Commission addresses standards.

## International Relations

NATO commitment remains absolute. EU relations reset with veterinary agreements and security cooperation, without rejoining single market or customs union. Palestinian statehood recognition is committed.
